record.title: 1-2-Switch
record.description: 1-2-Switch is a collection of 28 compact party activities created to demonstrate the original Nintendo Switch Joy-Con controllers. Many games deliberately ask players to stop watching the display and instead react to one another's body language, timing, sounds and controller feedback. Quick Draw turns two players into Wild West duelists; Milk uses repeated motion input; Ball Count demonstrates HD Rumble by simulating objects rolling inside the controller; Safe Crack asks players to rotate a Joy-Con while feeling subtle vibration feedback; Eating Contest uses the right Joy-Con's IR Motion Camera; Samurai Training, Sword Fight, Table Tennis, Wizard, Copy Dance and other activities explore motion, timing and social interaction. The title has no story campaign, progression economy or online multiplayer. Its value comes almost entirely from short face-to-face sessions with another person.

record.worldSummary: 1-2-Switch does not have a traditional story world. It is structured as a collection of short party scenarios presented through live-action-style prompts and simple visual feedback. The real focus is the physical space between the two players, with the television acting as an instruction and score display rather than the center of attention.
features: A face-to-face party-game format encourages players to watch each other instead of staring at the television.
A collection of short competitive activities demonstrates motion controls, HD Rumble and other Joy-Con functions.
Designed primarily around two-player local play with simple rules that can be explained quickly to new players.
Activities include reaction tests, duels, rhythm-like challenges and physical-comedy minigames.
The presentation is intentionally social, making spectators part of the experience even when they are not holding a controller.

record.title: A Plague Tale: Innocence - Cloud Version
record.titleEn: A Plague Tale: Innocence - Cloud Version
record.description:
Protect a younger brother while crossing a frightening, fictionalized fourteenth-century France. Amicia and Hugo face soldiers, ruined settlements and unnatural rat swarms in a linear adventure built around stealth, observation and environmental puzzles.

Amicia uses a sling, distractions and crafted alchemical ammunition. Light creates routes through the rats; darkness can turn an apparently safe passage into danger. Companions help with obstacles, while scavenged materials improve equipment. Optional gifts, curiosities and flowers reward exploration. The campaign contains 16 main chapters and an epilogue, rather than an open-world map.

This product is the Nintendo Switch CLOUD VERSION. The game runs on remote servers, not as a complete local installation. The Offline Account and Online Account labels describe the supplied account options; neither removes the internet requirement. Try the free launcher/demo using the intended connection and location before purchasing. The full game requires the appropriate paid access entitlement.

There is no physical Switch cartridge or genuine Switch retail box to include with this listing. This file leaves retail-front, back-cover and 3D-wrap fields empty deliberately; it uses real digital artwork and sourced imagery in their appropriate roles.

Nintendo lists multiple languages for its European release. The supplier account region and language restrictions still require confirmation. No Arabic localization is listed. Performance depends on the streaming service and connection; the reviews below are attributed historical reports, not a new hands-on benchmark.

record.description_short: A single-player stealth adventure following Amicia and Hugo through plague-stricken medieval France. Cloud streaming and continuous internet are required, including with the Offline Account option.
record.description_ar:
رافق أميسيا وأخيها الصغير هوغو في رحلة نجاة داخل فرنسا في القرن الرابع عشر، وسط الجنود والقرى المدمرة وأسراب الجرذان. تعتمد التجربة على التسلل، حل الألغاز البيئية، استخدام المقلاع والخيمياء، والتحكم بالضوء لتأمين الطريق. تجمع القصة الخطية بين التوتر والعلاقة الإنسانية بين الأخوين، مع مقتنيات ومواد لتطوير المعدات.

مهم: هذه نسخة سحابية وليست لعبة كاملة تعمل محليًا على الجهاز. يتطلب خيار «حساب أوفلاين» أيضًا اتصال إنترنت مستمرًا ومستقرًا؛ اسم الخيار يصف طريقة استخدام الحساب فقط. جرّب الديمو من موقعك وعلى اتصالك قبل الشراء، لأن توفر الخدمة وجودة البث قد يختلفان، ولم يُختبر تشغيلها من العراق ضمن هذا البحث.

اللعبة فردية ولا تدعم اللعب الجماعي، ولا يلزم اشتراك Nintendo Switch Online للبث نفسه. لا توجد خرطوشة سويتش فعلية أو غلاف علبة حقيقي لهذا الإصدار. العربية غير مدرجة ضمن اللغات الرسمية التي تم التحقق منها، ولم تُحدد منطقة حساب المورد بعد، لذلك لا يوجد تأكيد لقفل لغته أو غيابه.

تنبيه للمحتوى: اللعبة موجهة للبالغين، وتتضمن عنفًا شديدًا ومشاهد موت ومعاناة وجرذان ومحتوى قد يكون مزعجًا. مراجعة الأداء في الصفحة تشرح قيود البث وملاحظات المراجعين دون نسب أرقام 4K أو 60FPS الخاصة بمنصات أخرى إلى نسخة Switch.

record.nintendoNotes:
REFERENCE EDITION: Nintendo Europe; supplier account region is unconfirmed. European metadata lists English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, Korean and Chinese. It does not split every listed language into voice and text categories. English, French and German audio are documented for the original PC game; the exact voice menu on the supplied Switch cloud account has not been inspected. Do not promise a specific voice pack or absence of account-specific language restrictions without checking.

CLOUD ACCESS: Use the account carrying the paid access entitlement. A free launcher alone is not a purchase of the full game. Internet is mandatory; there is no multiplayer mode. Nintendo Switch Online membership is not needed for streaming, and its Save Data Cloud backup feature is not supported here.

SWITCH 2: Nintendo Europe currently lists backward compatibility as Supported, with no issues found. This is still a Switch 1 Cloud release, not a Nintendo Switch 2 Edition. No separate measured Switch 2 performance dataset was verified; hardware specifications are not game benchmarks.

MEDIA: The square image is official Switch Cloud artwork. Banners are distinct official promotional scenes. The gallery uses Nintendo's Switch product screenshots. Gameplay/world illustrations also include clearly credited community captures published by PlayStation Blog; these are not represented as Switch output. No genuine physical Switch box exists, so its front/back/3D fields are intentionally inapplicable.

TRADE-IN: There is no physical cartridge for trade-in. The numerical trade value of zero means no offer configured; no digital-account buyback commitment is promised.

All research was checked on 2026-08-28. Cloud service availability in Iraq, the supplied account entitlement and its region were not tested.

gameplayPillars.title: Observe before moving
gameplayPillars.description: Watch routes, cover and sightlines before crossing exposed ground. Direct confrontation is not the default solution; a carefully timed distraction can make a safer opening.

gameplayPillars.title: Protect Hugo
gameplayPillars.description: The journey links movement and decisions to the safety of Amicia's younger brother. Staying together and using companion assistance are part of progressing through obstacles.

gameplayPillars.title: Light against the swarm
gameplayPillars.description: Torches, braziers and other light sources establish safe space around the rats. Read the environment before committing to a route that may leave the children exposed.

gameplayPillars.title: The sling as a tool
gameplayPillars.description: Amicia's sling supports both combat and environmental interaction. Different situations ask for precise timing and ammunition choices rather than indiscriminate shooting.

gameplayPillars.title: Alchemy changes the route
gameplayPillars.description: Crafted ammunition can ignite or extinguish fires, distract threats or open opportunities. Unlocks broaden the available solutions as the story advances. Illustration: kuanpunchman, featured by PlayStation Blog (2021); not a Switch performance capture.

gameplayPillars.title: Companions and traversal
gameplayPillars.description: Allies contribute to obstacles and puzzles. Ruins, mechanisms and narrow routes interrupt the journey with tasks that require more than simply following a waypoint.

gameplayPillars.title: Scavenge and upgrade
gameplayPillars.description: Look for materials and workbenches to improve the sling, carrying capacity and crafting. Spending everything on consumables can delay useful equipment improvements.

gameplayPillars.title: Optional discoveries
gameplayPillars.description: Gifts, curiosities and Hugo's flowers add context beyond the main path. Chapter selection helps revisit missed discoveries; exploration remains within authored levels.

record.worldSummary:
The setting is a fictionalized France in 1348, shaped by war, plague and a supernatural mystery. Amicia and Hugo are children trying to survive these forces, not soldiers conquering a map. Their bond provides continuity as the route moves through villages, fields, churches, battlefields and ruined architecture.

The panels below explore characters and world themes without retelling the ending; they are editorial story sections, not a replacement for the game's chapter names. The complete chapter guide is linked separately. This is historical fantasy, not a documentary account of medieval events.

storyChapters.title: Amicia: learning to protect
storyChapters.body: Amicia becomes responsible for a vulnerable younger brother while confronting dangers far beyond her previous life. The story follows the emotional cost of that responsibility. Illustration: AloyUltra, featured in PlayStation Blog, 7 June 2019; a game-world image, not a Switch graphics benchmark.

storyChapters.title: The bond between siblings
storyChapters.body: Hugo and Amicia must learn how to rely on one another. Moments of trust and reassurance matter alongside escape sequences and threats. Illustration: tantfuriosa, featured in PlayStation Blog, 7 June 2019; a game-world image, not a Switch graphics benchmark.

storyChapters.title: Searching for shelter
storyChapters.body: An imposing castle can suggest safety, but the journey repeatedly asks what it takes to make a hostile place habitable. Refuge is a continuing need rather than a permanent guarantee. Illustration: IceWolfWarFare, featured in PlayStation Blog, 7 June 2019; a game-world image, not a Switch graphics benchmark.

storyChapters.title: The plague made visible
storyChapters.body: The rats are a supernatural threat as well as the central visual symbol of devastation. Their swarms turn architecture and darkness into immediate obstacles. Illustration: hokkai.do_ga, featured in PlayStation Blog, 7 June 2019; a game-world image, not a Switch graphics benchmark.

storyChapters.title: Violence beyond the rats
storyChapters.body: Human pursuers and the traces of war make the setting threatening even where the swarm is absent. The children navigate a society destabilized by fear. Illustration: tinymarsh_gamer, featured in PlayStation Blog, 7 June 2019; a game-world image, not a Switch graphics benchmark.

storyChapters.title: A fragile circle of light
storyChapters.body: Light offers temporary protection in a world where darkness may conceal danger. This recurring visual idea also underpins the environmental puzzles. Illustration: torqueman_captures, featured in PlayStation Blog, 7 June 2019; a game-world image, not a Switch graphics benchmark.

record.perfNotes:
PERFORMANCE REVIEW - NINTENDO SWITCH CLOUD VERSION

Architecture: Ubitus streams a remotely rendered game to the console. The launcher size is not the full game size. Stream quality, response and stability must be evaluated on the connection actually used. Neither the console's display resolution nor an uploaded video's resolution proves the game's rendering resolution. Sources: https://ubitus.ai/ubitus-assisted-with-focus-home-interactive-to-release-a-plague-tale-innocence-cloud-version-on-nintendo-switch-for-major-market-worldwide/ and https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Support/Purchases-Subscriptions/Games-Using-Cloud-Streaming-Technology-FAQ-1864576.html

Image clarity and startup: Nintendo World Report's review, published 12 August 2021, described a soft, muddy image, difficult small text and approximately two-and-a-half minutes from the HOME screen to gameplay. It also reported reloads after breaks, visible pop-in and occasional missing-ground glitches. These were that reviewer's observations, not guaranteed behavior today. Source: https://www.nintendoworldreport.com/review/58068/a-plague-tale-innocence-cloud-edition-switch-review

Connection variation: Rapid Reviews UK, published 22 August 2021, reported a generally successful streaming experience with occasional visual-quality drops when the connection weakened. Pure Nintendo, published 24 August 2021, reported slow loads and inactivity timeouts, including during waits, while still enjoying the game. These differing reports support testing rather than promising uniform results. Sources: https://www.rapidreviewsuk.com/a-plague-tale-innocence-making-the-switch-cloud-version/ and https://purenintendo.com/review-a-plague-tale-innocence-cloud-version-nintendo-switch/

Handheld and TV: both modes are supported, but neither mode removes network dependence. No defensible current per-mode FPS range, exact stream resolution, bitrate, latency measurement, dynamic-resolution behavior or server graphics preset was verified. Those numeric/boolean fields remain unset where necessary. The published PS5/Xbox 4K and 60 FPS upgrade claims are not Switch Cloud measurements.

Practical recommendation: use the free demo at the intended location, check responsiveness and dark-scene clarity, and test a longer session before paying. Do not rely on sleep mode as if the remote session were a locally suspended game. A successful test does not guarantee future connection quality. Iraq service availability and the supplied account were not tested.

Evidence reviewed on 2026-08-28. No original hands-on performance test was conducted for this file. No unverified Switch patch number is assigned.

faq.q: Can I play the Offline Account option without internet?
faq.a: No. Offline Account is the merchant's account-use label. This Cloud Version still needs a stable, continuous internet connection.

faq.q: Is this a native Nintendo Switch port?
faq.a: No. A small launcher connects to a remotely running game. The full game is not installed locally.

faq.q: Is the free download the complete purchased game?
faq.a: No. The launcher/trial checks the service; full play requires the appropriate paid access entitlement.

faq.q: Should I test it before purchase?
faq.a: Yes. Try the free demo from your intended location and connection. Cloud availability and quality in Iraq were not verified in this research.

faq.q: Does Nintendo Switch Online membership replace the access pass?
faq.a: No. Streaming itself does not require Nintendo Switch Online, and that membership does not buy this game's access entitlement.

faq.q: Does internet access mean this is a multiplayer game?
faq.a: No. It is a one-player adventure. There is no co-op, competitive, split-screen or local-wireless mode.

faq.q: Is the game locked to Chinese?
faq.a: No Chinese-only restriction is established by the evidence. Nintendo Europe lists several languages. The supplied account's region and restrictions remain unconfirmed, so an unrestricted-language guarantee is not made.

faq.q: Is Arabic supported?
faq.a: Arabic is not listed among the checked official languages.

faq.q: Which voice languages are guaranteed for this account?
faq.a: The supplier account voice menu has not been inspected. English speech is evidenced in Switch material. The original PC game lists English, French and German voices, but that list should not be assumed to confirm every Switch account.

faq.q: Can I play in handheld or TV mode?
faq.a: Yes. Nintendo lists handheld, tabletop and TV modes; all continue to require cloud connectivity.

faq.q: Will it work on Nintendo Switch 2?
faq.a: Nintendo lists backward compatibility as supported. This does not make the product a Switch 2 Edition or establish improved frame rate/resolution.

faq.q: Does it support 4K and 60 FPS on Switch?
faq.a: Those claims in the 2021 announcement concern PS5/Xbox enhancements. No verified per-mode Switch resolution/FPS pair is assigned here.

faq.q: What happens when I pause or use sleep mode?
faq.a: Historical Switch reviews report server timeouts and reconnect/loading delays after breaks. Do not treat the remote session as guaranteed local suspend/resume.

faq.q: Is Nintendo Switch Online Save Data Cloud supported?
faq.a: Nintendo explicitly lists that backup feature as unsupported for this software; server-run gameplay is a different use of cloud technology.

faq.q: How much storage is needed?
faq.a: The checked Nintendo Europe page lists an 87.0 MB launcher download. A separate exact required-free-space figure was not published there.

faq.q: How long is the campaign?
faq.a: Plan roughly 12-15 hours for a first campaign according to Rapid Reviews UK. Completion time varies with exploration, replay and cloud loading; the numeric 13/15-hour values are planning estimates.

faq.q: Are the score fields based on the Switch edition?
faq.a: The four selected reviews cover the Switch Cloud release. Their normalized arithmetic mean is 8.1/10. No unverified Switch-specific Metacritic, OpenCritic or user aggregate is substituted.

faq.q: Does this offer include DLC or Requiem?
faq.a: Neither a separate Switch DLC entitlement nor Requiem is confirmed in the supplied offer. Only the base Innocence cloud game is listed.

faq.q: Can I receive or trade a physical Switch cartridge?
faq.a: No physical cartridge is part of this cloud product. No trade-in offer is configured; the zero value is not a used-cartridge valuation.

faq.q: Is it appropriate for young children?
faq.a: The checked ratings are PEGI 18 and ESRB Mature. Expect intense violence, death, distressing situations, strong language and frightening rat swarms.

faq.q: Can I return later for missed collectibles?
faq.a: The game has chapter selection. Collection guides can help revisit discoveries; equipment-upgrade planning may still require replaying material-gathering sections.

record.verdictSummary:
Review roundup: 8.1/10 is the arithmetic mean of four identified Switch Cloud reviews, with Rapid Reviews UK's 4.5/5 normalized to 9/10. This is a sourced editorial summary, not a new test.

The attraction is a focused story, memorable atmosphere and the interaction between stealth, light and the rat swarms. The trade-off is reliance on a live cloud service: reviewers differ on clarity and smoothness, and several mention loading or timeout friction. For this edition, a successful local demo test matters more than an attractive specification borrowed from another console.

No separately verified Switch-specific Metacritic, OpenCritic or user aggregate is assigned. The original PC game's Metacritic listing and the broader OpenCritic page do not establish a Cloud Version score. All performance observations in this file retain their source and historical context.
verdictPros: Strong atmosphere and carefully staged environments.
Light and rat swarms give environmental puzzles a distinct identity.
Voice performances and music support the dramatic tone.
Stealth, crafting and exploration complement the narrative.
A free trial allows checking cloud suitability before purchase.
verdictCons: Continuous internet and live service access are mandatory.
Visual clarity can deteriorate with the stream.
Historical reviews report slow startup and reloads.
Idle timeouts can interrupt the pace.
Portability depends on a suitable connection, not only battery life.
No local offline installation or physical Switch cartridge.
No verified per-mode Switch performance measurements are supplied.

The Nintendo Switch version brings the original game to handheld, tabletop and TV play.

record.worldSummary: Bayonetta awakens with fragmented memories and is drawn into a conflict involving the Umbra Witches, Lumen Sages and celestial forces. Her journey across Vigrid gradually reconstructs her past while escalating into increasingly extravagant battles.

storyChapters.title: The Witch Awakens
storyChapters.body: Bayonetta fights angels while searching for the truth behind her lost memories.

storyChapters.title: Vigrid and the Past
storyChapters.body: The journey through Vigrid reveals links to the Umbra Witches, Lumen Sages and Bayonetta’s origin.

storyChapters.title: The Eyes of the World
storyChapters.body: The conflict expands into a struggle over ancient powers tied to the balance of the world.

storyChapters.title: Climax
storyChapters.body: The story culminates in the series’ signature mixture of supernatural mythology and oversized action spectacle.

faq.q: Does Bayonetta work on Nintendo Switch 2?
faq.a: Yes through backward compatibility where Nintendo marks the Nintendo Switch release as supported. This file does not classify it as a native Nintendo Switch 2 Edition.

faq.q: What language is the supplier version of Bayonetta?
faq.a: Supplier listing language supplied by the user: English. Official/regional language details are preserved separately in supported_languages_raw and nintendo_notes so the supplier SKU is not generalized to every region.

faq.q: Is Bayonetta multiplayer?
faq.a: The main game is single-player; no multiplayer mode is asserted in this file.

faq.q: Why are some Switch 2 performance resolution fields blank for Bayonetta?
faq.a: Because exact measured Switch 2 backward-compatibility rendering values were not verified. The template is intentionally left blank rather than filled with hardware maximums or guesses.

record.verdictSummary: A foundational stylish-action game with unusually deep combat and enduring replay value. The Switch port is technically modest in resolution but remains a strong way to play the original on a portable Nintendo system.
